about.title: Calabasas Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and Calabasas families are not immune to that reality. Behind each of those numbers is a household now facing funeral costs, lost income, and an absence no paperwork can fill. LawProactive is not a law firm, but a free service that connects grieving families with an independent personal injury attorney who understands how California's wrongful death statute works. If someone you love died because of another party's negligence on a Calabasas road, an attorney in our network can review what happened and explain your options, with no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: What Calabasas Families Should Know About Wrongful Death Law

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible under narrower circumstances. An attorney can help clarify who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Starts at Two Years
items.desc: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter deadline. Acting sooner rather than later helps preserve evidence and protect your options.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond Funeral Costs
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case that may also arise from the same incident.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Calabasas?
items.answer: Under California law, families generally have two years from the date of death to file. If a government entity, such as a public road agency, may be involved, that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just months. It's worth speaking with an attorney early to avoid missing any filing window.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they are separate proceedings. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by eligible family members seeking compensation for their losses. One can proceed regardless of the outcome of the other.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on US-101 or a city street like Calabasas Road?
items.answer: The location itself doesn't change the family's legal rights, but it can affect who may be responsible, whether that's another driver, a government entity for road conditions, or another party. An attorney will look closely at where and how the collision occurred to identify every potentially liable party.
